leadText: Pokémon The Movie: White—Victini and Zekrom (Japanese: ビクティニと き ゼクロム Victini and the Black Hero: Zekrom) is the adaptation of the movie of the same name. It is adapted by Momota Inoue. It was serialized in CoroCoro Comics.
plainText:
Pokémon The Movie: White—Victini and Zekrom (Japanese: ビクティニと き ゼクロム Victini and the Black Hero: Zekrom) is the adaptation of the movie of the same name. It is adapted by Momota Inoue. It was serialized in CoroCoro Comics.

==Publications==
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

==Chapters==
The Mythical Pokémon of Eindoak
Here Comes Zekrom

==Differences between the movie and the manga==
At the beginning of the movie, Damon is able to convince the people in the desert village his intentions are noble after he summons and saves the village from a twister and a stampede of . In the manga, the possible disaster is removed and Damon is able to convince the villagers of his honesty by simply summoning Reshiram.
saves two at the beginning of the movie, while at the beginning of the manga, he only saves one.
Mannes's , , and are not present in the manga.
While in the movie enters the Eindoak Town tournament with her and enters with his , in the manga, they simply cheer on while he competes (thereby removing their most significant role from the story).
While Ash's Scraggy remains outside his throughout the Eindoak Town tournament in the movie (where he provides a lot of comic moments), in the manga he is only sent out to face Carlita's .
In the movie, the People of the Vale from both the arctic and the desert travel to Eindoak Town in support of Damon's plan, while in the manga, only the people of the desert come to Eindoak Town.

==Translation edits==
===Errors===
At the end of the translated version of the manga, the title is erroneously listed as Pokémon the Movie: White—Victini and Reshiram.
